name: Shechem
overview: Shechem is a male figure from the tribe of Manasseh, identified uniquely as the son of Shemida according to 1 Chronicles 7:19. Beyond this paternal link, Scripture provides no further details about his life or role. His mention situates him within the genealogical records important for understanding Israel's tribal heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Shechem means 'shoulders and upper part of the back' or possibly 'shoulder' as in 'saddle of a hill,' reflecting a geographical or physical characteristic. This proper name was not given by God but carries descriptive significance as recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shechem as the son of Shemida, establishing his immediate paternal relationship. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Shechem's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical lineage of the tribe of Manasseh, serving as a link in the ancestral chain recorded in 1 Chronicles. While not elaborated upon in narrative events, his mention contributes to the biblical record of God's providential preservation of His chosen people through successive generations.
